אַרְכִּין ה׳ שְׁמַיָּא — Arkin Hashem Shemaya, a piyyut narrating the ascent of Mosheh (Yiddish translation, 1694)

tei:bibl.tei:title: ארכין ער נײגט גאט דען הימל אױף בּערג סיני
אַרְכִּין ה׳ שְׁמַיָּא — Arkin Hashem Shemaya, a piyyut narrating the ascent of Mosheh (Yiddish translation, 1694)
tei:bibl.tei:note: Converted from the export of opensiddur.org at 624215eef0.

tei:div.tei:p: This is “Arkin Hashem Shemaya l’Sinai,” an Aramaic piyyut from late Antiquity by an unknown author, with a Yiddish translation from 1694. The Aramaic source text of Arkin provided here is the critical text offered in Shirat Bene Ma’arava: Jewish Palestinian Aramaic from Antiquity [Hebrew], edited and translated by Joseph Yahalom and Michael Sokoloff (Jerusalem: Israel Academy of Sciences and Humanities, 1999) and shared online via the Comprehensive Aramaic Lexicon.

The Yiddish translation is appended to the first known printing of the Maaséh Aqdamut (Fürth 1694). The transcription is based on an earlier transcription of the Fürth 1694 printing published by Isaac Rivkind in “די היסטאָרישע אַלעגאָריע פון ר׳ מאיר שַ״ץ” (“The Historical Allegory of Rabbi Meir, shatz [Shaliaḥ Tsibur]”) the first chapter in Filologishe shriftn vol. 3 (1929), pp. 1-42. (This translation of the Aqdamut appears on pages/numbered columns 40-42.) This translation was followed by a Yiddish translation of “Aqdamut Milin,” another Aramaic piyyut still read by many Ashkenazi communities on Shavuot.
